topic: Using different Synthetic test frequencies on weekdays and weekends to reduce cost
symptom_pattern: Customer wants a URL check to run as often as possible during the working day, but only every 10 minutes on weekends and out-of-office periods to reduce cost. They ask whether one Synthetic test can do this.
root_cause: This is a product limitation, not a fault. A single Synthetic test has one fixed execution frequency, so it can't vary by day of the week.
resolution_path: Confirmed a single Synthetic test cannot use different frequencies by day of week.
Suggested creating two otherwise identical tests: a higher-frequency weekday test active Monday–Friday and a lower-frequency weekend test active Saturday–Sunday.
Said the setup could reduce cost because it means fewer total executions.

qa_pairs.tse_question: Asked whether there was anything else they could help with.
qa_pairs.customer_answer: The customer asked whether the two-test setup would reduce cost.

evidence: A single Datadog Synthetic test has one fixed execution frequency
Weekday test: Higher frequency, active Monday–Friday.
Weekend test: Lower frequency, active Saturday–Sunday.

tse_approach.summary: The engineer answered a how-to question in chat. They first said it was probably not possible, then confirmed after a follow-up that one test has a single fixed frequency. They offered a two-test workaround and said it could reduce cost.
steps: Gave an initial answer that this likely isn't possible and two tests might be needed.
Confirmed that a single test has one fixed execution frequency when the customer asked again.
Described the workaround of two otherwise identical tests with weekday and weekend schedules.
Answered the cost follow-up by saying savings would come from fewer total executions.
key_questions: Asked whether there was anything else they could help with, which led to the cost question.
communication: Gave short, direct answers. Presented the workaround as a bulleted list contrasting the weekday and weekend tests. Hedged the cost answer with 'potentially'.
